props.title: Knowledge grows when we build it together.
props.caption: Stanisław Ulam · illustrated portrait
paragraphs: In the cafés of Lwów, Stanisław Ulam and fellow mathematicians discussed problems and recorded them in a shared notebook: the Scottish Book. Questions, solutions and new ideas grew through collaboration.
Ulam later translated the collection so it could reach more people, inviting readers to contribute corrections and further developments.
props.connection: That spirit inspires ULAMS: turn your organisation’s documents into shared learning, work with people and agents, and keep improving the knowledge together. Open source, free to use and open to contribution.

source.label: The Scottish Book · Ulam’s preface, University of St Andrews

more.label: More questions on the FAQ page

items.a: ULAMS is an open-source LMS for organisations, universities and technical teams. Its headless API supports branded learning sites, course authoring and integrations.
Yes. ULAMS is MIT licensed. You provide hosting; paid AI provider calls, if enabled, are billed by your chosen provider. H5P runs as a separate service with its own GPL licence.

items.q: Can I try the whole stack locally?
items.a: Yes. Install the CLI and run ulams stack up with Docker Compose available. The development trial uses deterministic AI responses without paid model calls. Node.js 22.12 or newer is required.

Use Docker Compose on your own server or native Kubernetes manifests on an existing cluster. A VPS or virtual machine on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure can host the stack. Production needs DNS, HTTPS and persistent storage.
The CLI and MCP interface let compatible agents work with the platform. You can use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini CLI, or integrate directly through the REST API.

items.q: Does AI publish a course automatically?
items.a: No. AI prepares a draft with source citations. The author reviews the outline and content, then approves publication. Production starts with AI disabled until you configure a provider.

items.q: Can each academy use its own brand and domain?
items.a: Yes. Each tenant has its own learning site, theme and isolated database. The initial academy is created by the stack launcher; additional tenants use the platform tenant workflow.

items.q: How do I stop it without losing courses?
items.a: Run ulams stack down. Data and credentials remain available when you run stack up again in the same installation directory. Only stack down --purge --yes deliberately removes persistent data.
